title: Are Large Language Models Strategic Decision Makers? A Study of Performance and Bias in Two-Player Non-Zero-Sum Games

bias_targets.methodology: Changing the order in which action labels (e.g., A and B) are presented in the prompt's game description to evaluate if the model systematically favors the first or second option.

Altering the payoffs associated with different action labels to test if the model is systematically drawn to actions offering the maximum possible self-gain or common-gain, rather than logically maximizing the expected gain.

Modifying the prompted preferred behavior of the players (e.g., prioritizing Common-Gain versus Self-Gain) to observe if the model rigidly anchors to a specific action label irrespective of the opponent's behavior.
